note: Golden vectors for the Finance Engine. The server test runs these against functions/finance/engine.js; every platform's mirror must run the same file and produce the same numbers. Adding a case here is how a rule becomes real. Spec: docs/finance-engine.md.

cases.name: decision example: standard VAT is extracted from the price the customer pays
cases.why: NivaDesk_Urun_Kararlari_20260903.md §2 — £120 at 20% is £20 of VAT, not £24.

cases.name: decision example: the margin scheme deducts the purchase price and nothing else
cases.why: Purchase 1500, sale 2000, margin 500, VAT 500 x 1/6 = 83.33. The old Profit type also deducted the fee, the shipping and every expense, which declared less VAT than the scheme allows.

cases.name: decision example: gross margin is revenue less direct cost
cases.why: Revenue 2000, product cost 1200, gross margin 800. Fees and shipping are not part of it.

cases.name: the composite order the survey used against all five old implementations
cases.why: Paid 1500 + remaining 500 + a listed receivable 200 + an orphan receivable 100; purchase 1200; fee 3%; shipping 20; expenses 150 and -50; margin scheme at 20%. Every old layer produced a different number for this order.

cases.name: hiding the base cost in the card settings does not change a single figure
cases.why: The product decision is explicit: UI visibility is separate from accounting. The web and Swift both removed the base cost from profit when it was hidden.

cases.name: a refund reduces the profit
cases.why: The decision lists refunds and adjustments as a deduction. No platform deducted refundedAmount.

cases.name: a negative expense is a credit and raises the profit
cases.why: The server turned every amount at or below zero into zero; the clients kept the sign. Clamping silently changed money.

cases.name: an amount with no heading still counts, and is reported
cases.why: Swift and one of the two web rules dropped it, so a total came out smaller than the rows it was built from.

cases.name: a workspace that is not VAT registered owes nothing whatever the rate says
prices quoted without VAT add it on top
cases.why: Every workspace today is inclusive, which is why the default stays inclusive. This is the new setting.

cases.name: invoice lines decide what the order is worth
cases.why: The line-items-only rule the invoice renderers already follow.

cases.name: selling at a loss under the margin scheme owes no VAT
the order's own method overrides the workspace default
before the tax milestone the margin scheme applies
cases.why: financialTaxTypeForPaymentDate has always switched method on this date; the engine keeps it.

cases.name: on and after the tax milestone the standard scheme applies
an amount stored in another platform's format is read as the person meant it
cases.why: Values reached customFields from text fields on four platforms over two years.

cases.name: the platform fee follows the revenue, including the custom receivables
an empty order is all zeros rather than NaN
